gaps.sentence: The new model has ___ moving parts, so it breaks down less often.
gaps.explanation: 'Fewer moving parts' is correct because 'parts' is countable and plural.

gaps.sentence: ___ the food was eaten within minutes.
gaps.explanation: 'All the food' is correct with an uncountable noun; 'whole' needs 'the whole of' and 'both' needs two separate items.

gaps.sentence: Does the project need ___ more work?
gaps.explanation: 'Work' is uncountable here, so 'much more work' is correct; 'many more work' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: This is ___ beautiful beach on the island.
gaps.explanation: 'The most beautiful' is the superlative form used for comparisons within a group.

gaps.sentence: We see our grandparents ___ other weekend.
gaps.explanation: 'Every other weekend' means alternate weekends; 'each other' has a different, reciprocal meaning.
'Luggage' is an uncountable noun, so 'how much' is used.

gaps.hint: price per item comes at the end
gaps.explanation: 'Fifteen pounds each' means fifteen pounds per ticket; 'every' cannot stand alone in this position.

gaps.sentence: There isn't ___ room in here for a piano.
gaps.explanation: 'Enough room' means sufficient space; the negative 'isn't' shows the space is insufficient.
